title: Steering context is assumed delivered, and nothing verifies that it was
problem: I wrote the instruction that would have prevented this failure, it was in the file the agent is supposed to read, and it never reached the model.
symptom: The agent repeats a mistake that is explicitly addressed in its steering file; inspecting the file shows the text present, so the steering looks correct.
why_now: Steering is injected through a consumer-side transform (a digest, a summariser, a bounded window) whose truncation and parsing rules are invisible to the author. Authoring and delivery are never tested as separate things.
existing: Prompt logging: shows the final prompt but only if you look, and usually after the loss.
Character or token budgets: exist, but silently cut and are read from the newest source rather than the running version.
Convention files that tools auto-read: still subject to the same truncation, with no receipt.

evidence.title: INC-0020: a steering channel counts only when the consumer's own parser emits it
evidence.quote: A steering channel counts as delivered only when the CONSUMER's own parser emits it - verify by calling that parser, not by inspecting the file.
evidence.note: Also records the specific trap of reading the budget from the newest source rather than the version actually running.

evidence.title: INC-0004: a monotonically growing required-reading file silently kills the loop
evidence.quote: Any file injected into EVERY iteration's prompt is a resource. Bound it by CHARACTERS, not item count, and cap it at write time.
evidence.note: The same channel fails in the opposite direction when unbounded: the log then resembles a rate-limit stall, so the cause is misattributed.

build_hypothesis: A delivery receipt: call the consumer's own digest function on the steering file, assert a caller-supplied marker survives, and fail the run loudly at startup if it does not.

check.manual_question: You inject a steering file into agent prompts. What asserts that it is actually DELIVERED to the model rather than truncated or dropped by the consumer's own digest?
check.rationale: A steering file with no test naming it has never been proven to reach the model. This is the cheapest real check in the register: it compares the existence of a steering artifact against any test that mentions it.
